BOSCOOpen dashboard ↗

PROJECT GUIDE

Observe. Review. Coordinate.

BOSCO / Emberwatch combines ANAFI camera and telemetry, fire detection, illustrative spread, rescue leads and Gemini-assisted planning.

StartData flowSource mapReplayVerificationTeam docs

Start the dashboard

npm ci
# Copy .env.example to .env and set two distinct local tokens.
npm start

Use Node 22+. Open the dashboard through the local backend. Live mode waits for aircraft input; it does not create sample observations. Gemini and TigerData are optional server-side configuration.

Hardware reception needs a separate configured receiver. Observation sends no aircraft commands. Explicit terminal flight modes have different triggers and limits; read the selected workflow before enabling execution.

Follow the data

ANAFI → Pi/Linux receiver → authenticated backend
                            → video + evidence storage
                            → Gemini analysis / plan
                            → dashboard → human review → export

Simulation → separate replay API/UI
Operator terminal → explicit flight runtime → aircraft

The laptop keeps Internet access while Pi Wi-Fi joins the aircraft. The backend and browser do not provide a flight-command channel.

Source map

PathResponsibility
backend/HTTP, validation, storage, Gemini and person-search logic
dist/Plain JavaScript dashboard, map and simulated camera; no build step
bridge/Reception, detection, calibration and separate flight runtimes
scripts/Laptop setup, Pi deployment, launch and recording review
tests/Isolated services, geometry and guarded SDK checks

The API contract is emberwatch.v1. Ingest and dashboard tokens differ. Unknown GPS remains unknown; altitude is height above takeoff. Person leads include location uncertainty and require a named reviewer.

Demonstrate without an aircraft

npm run demo
npm run demo -- --port 9000

Replay offers person-search scenarios, historical fire/camera cases and an animated flight pattern. Choose a case, inspect its evidence and coverage, then exit replay to return to live monitoring.

Gemini replay requests use the configured real service, but their results stay out of live storage. Without a key the UI reports unavailability.

Check what is actually known

npm test
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p '*_test.py'

Python SDK checks may skip without Olympe. Tests use fixtures/mock aircraft; they do not fly or validate field accuracy. A configured key, retained image or sent landing command is not proof of a successful live operation.

Spread is illustrative. Rescue positions and Gemini output are estimates; a human reviews plans. Store flight footage locally and record physical and cloud-service checks separately.

Team documentation

In the repository, start with README.md and TEAM_AI_CONTEXT.md. The docs/ directory contains focused Windows/Mac, API, calibration and flight workflows.
